newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 7.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Finance Minister S A M S Kibria said on Tuesday the facility of reshceduling of bank loans had become a "camouflage for not repaying money to the banks".
The District Judge's court on Wednesday stayed the proceedings of the murder case of independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman till June 10, in compliance with a High Court order.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Tuesday said her government had taken diplomatic initiatives to resolve all outstanding issues with the neighbouring countries through peaceful negotiations.
The ensuing national budget will focus on a "growth with equity" startegy to be reflected in the government's agenda of action for development, Finance Minister S A M S Kibria said on Tuesday.

General Secretary of the ruling Awami League, Zilur Rahman, told the party's national convention on Tuesday that Awami League would implement its election pledges for establishing a pro-people, accountable and transparent government.
The government has decided to set up a Taka 52 crore planetorium, to be named after independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, to let the scientists and students know about astronomical science.
A private power developer, the New England Corporation, has offered electricity tariff cheaper than the state-run Power Development Board.

Discovery of large reserves of natural gas, relative political calm and actions to encourage foreign investment have led to ten-fold increase of American investment in Bangladesh in past six months, the U.S. envoy in Dhaka said on Tuesday. REUTER
